text:
A clear night
of festivity and moonlight,
night of my dreams,
night of joy

—my soul was light
that today is all mist,
my hair was not
black yet—,

the youngest fairy
carried me in her arms
to the joyful festival
that blazed in the square.

Beneath the crackling
of the lights,
love wove its skeins
of dances.

And on that night
of festivity and moonlight,
night of my dreams,
night of joy,

the youngest fairy
kissed my brow…
with her lovely hand
she bade me farewell…

All the rosebushes
gave their fragrances,
all loves,
Love half-opened them.

translation.title: Childhood Dream
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Machado's refrain, the fairy's farewell, the poem's ellipses, and its movement from remembered light to present mist.
